correctness.rationale: The exact Euclidean Lorentz-cone projection formula is differentiated on its three open regions. The intermediate Jacobian J=1/2 [[1,u^T],[u,(1+t)I-tuu^T]] has a scalar row of norm at most (1+sqrt d)/2 and spatial rows bounded sharply by 1+max g_d(a)/2. Strict negativity of g_d second derivative gives a unique maximizer; direct test proves spatial dominance for d=2..4, and the exact bound g_5(a)<sqrt5-1 combined with monotonicity in d proves scalar dominance for all d>=5. A segmentwise integration argument provides the global Lipschitz upper bound and local derivatives, including t tending to one, prove sharpness. The self-contained checker passed 5,461 finite assertions; those finite checks corroborate the analytical proof but are not themselves universal certificates. All formulas specify real d>=1, standard cone aperture and an Euclidean minimizer measured in ell_infinity.

value.rationale: Euclidean cone projection is standard in conic optimization, but coordinatewise error propagation is not governed by Hilbert nonexpansivity. The exact all-dimensional condition number and strict dimension-five transition identify a natural stability boundary: spatial output coordinates control worst-case amplification at d=2,3,4, while the scalar output controls it for every d>=5. The low-dimensional extremizing direction is unique up to symmetries and sharp constants are provided via uniquely defined algebraic root equations. This is a complete, motivated classification rather than a numerical fit or arbitrary finite slice; limitations are the unweighted standard cone and the specified error metric.
